headline: Highest risk is none-to-low overall: both agents are docs-only, local-only, and lack shared channels or write/network capabilities, so pairwise injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are largely blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default injection bridge is documented. agent_a has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or network surfaces, and agent_b likewise shows no shared channel or parsing surface. Without a bridge, agent_a cannot feed attacker-controlled content into agent_b as instructions.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP server, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_b begins parsing agent_a output as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared clipboard and shared folders.
Disable any future MCP bridge unless provenance tracking is added.
Require explicit human review before copying outputs between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles do not show sensitive data classes, shared workspace, or outbound transmission. agent_a has no filesystem read/write and no network egress; agent_b also has no network egress. With no documented data flow, leakage between them is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_b is configured to upload memory or context to a backend, reassess.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Review any future logging or export settings before enabling them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. agent_a cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and agent_b exposes no write, git, or network capability in the profile. Without shared mutable resources, capability conflict is effectively blocked.
conditions: IF agent_b is later granted filesystem or git write access, conflict risk should be re-evaluated.
IF both agents are placed over the same mutable directory, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Avoid mounting the same writable directory into both agents.
Use separate workspaces for any future write-enabled deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error path is only weakly plausible because agent_a is document-processing and agent_b is knowledge-management, but neither profile shows downstream action authority or a documented trust pipeline. The pair lacks evidence that agent_b will treat agent_a output as authoritative by default.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to ingest agent_a outputs without verification, the risk rises.
IF either agent is connected to an action-taking workflow, reassess for higher impact.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agent_a and agent_b.
Require citations or source links on any transferred facts.
Limit agent_b to summarization unless outputs are reviewed.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. Both profiles are docs-only and show no data classes touched, so there is no evidenced compliance pathway to compare.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be rechecked.
IF retention or residency settings are introduced, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Add retention and residency settings to the runbook.
Review legal/compliance requirements before enabling regulated workloads.
